title: Fine-grained descending control of steering in walking Drosophila.
source_locator: Results, "Different descending neurons drive distinctive leg gestures"; Fig. 4A-4C
quote: In experimental flies, we found that a pulse of light triggered an ipsilateral turn, with no change in forward velocity as compared with controls
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNa02 is a MANC/Namiki type name listed in type_list.csv; genotype R75C10AD/R87D07DBD corresponds to SS00730 (DNa02 in driver_lines.csv).
stimulation: 620/60 nm light, 0.09 mW/mm2, 200 ms pulses (2 s pulses also tested, similar transient effect)
type_coverage: one of the two DNa02 cells (unilateral SPARC expression)
sensory_condition: tethered on spherical treadmill, walking; norpA mutant background (blind)
other_cell_types: a single type of visual neuron with arbors in the lobula (~2 cells per hemisphere)
a few cells in the abdominal ganglion
coordination_notes: Stride length of all three ipsilateral legs decreased, mainly via a shortened return stroke; step direction of front and middle legs shifted bilaterally into the turn
n_flies_note: n=8 CsChrimson+ flies and 7 no-CsChrimson control flies
notes: Stimulation trials were only analysed if the fly was already walking (forward velocity >=1 mm/s around stimulation), so leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed per PROTOCOL section 3 (turning/speed change in an already-walking fly). Leg kinematics were tracked in detail (stride length, return/power stroke).

title: Fine-grained descending control of steering in walking Drosophila.
source_locator: Results, "Different descending neurons drive distinctive leg gestures"; Fig. S6A-S6C
quote: Bilateral activation of DNa02 instead triggered a decrease in forward velocity without a change in the heading direction (Figure S6A).
mapping_basis: The paper's name DNa02 is a MANC/Namiki type name listed in type_list.csv; genotype R75C10AD/R87D07DBD corresponds to SS00730 (DNa02 in driver_lines.csv).
sensory_condition: tethered on spherical treadmill, walking; norpA mutant background (blind)
other_cell_types: a single type of visual neuron with arbors in the lobula (~2 cells per hemisphere)
a few cells in the abdominal ganglion
coordination_notes: Bilateral stimulation produced the same leg movement changes as unilateral stimulation, but bilaterally: shortened stride length via a shortened return stroke, little effect on the power stroke
n_flies_note: n=3 CsChrimson+ (bilateral) flies and 7 no-CsChrimson control flies
notes: Separate experiment from the unilateral record: flies with SPARC expression in both DNa02 copies. Only already-walking trials analysed, so leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed per PROTOCOL section 3; the fly slowed but stepping was not reported to start or stop. Related text: "Bilateral stimulation produced the same leg movement changes, except bilaterally instead of unilaterally (Figures S6B and S6C)."

title: A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila.
source_locator: Results, "Stationarity is necessary and sufficient to drive vibrations in males"; Fig. 3C, 3D
quote: Conversely, inducing female walking by optogenetically activating the DNp28 neurons55,56 nearly abolished vibrations (Fig. 3C, D).
mapping_basis: Paper names DNp28 (a MANC type in type_list.csv) and cites Namiki 2018/Bidaye 2020; but its stated line SS01587 is mapped to DNp29 in driver_lines.csv, so the name-to-line pairing is inconsistent and confidence is capped at medium.
stimulation: 625 nm red LED, 89 mW/cm2, 5 s stimulation per trial, 30 trials
sensory_condition: freely walking in a 44 mm behavioural chamber while being courted by a wild-type male
n_flies_note: DNp28-Chrimson+ N = 9 pairs; controls DNp28-Gal4+ N = 4, UAS-Chrimson+ N = 5, DNp28-Chrimson- N = 7
notes: Walking/acceleration was scored from centroid velocity tracking, not leg tracking, so leg rhythms are inferred from walking per PROTOCOL section 3 and labeler_confidence is capped at medium. Fig. 3C legend: "Optogenetic activation (gray) of DNp28 neurons in a female courted by a wild-type male accelerates the pair". The paper's purpose was the male's signalling; the female's locomotion is the manipulated variable.
